title: Cape Reinga & Ninety Mile Beach Family Day Tour – Honest Review
meta_desc: Find out if the Cape Reinga and Ninety Mile Beach day tour is worth it for families. Costs, age suitability, tips, best time to go and how to book.
intro: The Cape Reinga and Ninety Mile Beach tour is a classic Northland bucket‑list item, but how does it hold up when you’re travelling with kids? We spent a full day on the bus from Pahia and broke down the highs, the lows and the hidden tricks to make it family‑friendly.

sections.heading: What the day looks like
sections.body:
The tour kicks off around 8 am from either Pahia (about a 3‑hour drive north of Auckland) or Kaitaia (roughly 4 hours). After a scenic drive along State Highway 1 you’ll turn onto the hard‑sand track that becomes the road to Ninety Mile Beach – the bus is literally your only vehicle on the sand.

Highlights include a quick stop at the Te Paki sand dunes where you can try sand‑boarding (equipment is provided), a lunch break at a local café, and the final walk to the iconic Cape Reinga lighthouse where the Tasman Sea meets the Pacific. The whole experience runs 9‑10 hours, so bring snacks, water and a good pair of sunglasses.

sections.heading: Kids and age suitability
sections.body:
The operator lists a minimum age of 5 years, which is realistic – younger children can find the long bus ride and the walk to the lighthouse tiring. Most families with kids aged 6‑12 find the sand‑boarding and the open beach space a hit.

That said, the drive can be bumpy and the sand‑track feels a bit like a roller‑coaster for nervous little ones. Bring a small travel pillow and consider a light snack to keep energy levels up.
list: Best for ages 6‑12 (younger can join but may need extra breaks)
Bring a hat and sunscreen – the beach is exposed
Pack a change of clothes – sand gets everywhere

sections.heading: Cost and value for money
sections.body:
At $99 per adult and $70 per child the price is mid‑range for a full‑day Northland tour, but you’re paying for transport on the beach, a sand‑boarding session and a guide who points out Māori legends and wildlife.

For a typical family of two adults and two children the total comes to $338, which includes lunch (usually a simple sandwich pack). Compared with hiring a private 4WD for the day (easily $400‑$600), the bus option is cheaper and eliminates the stress of navigating the sand.

sections.heading: Insider tips & best time to visit
sections.body:
The tour runs year‑round, but the most pleasant weather is from late spring to early autumn (October‑April). Summer can be hot and the beach winds up with more tourists, while winter brings cooler breezes that can make the sand‑track feel slippery.

Book early in the school holidays – spots fill up fast – and ask the operator if they have a “family discount” for groups of four or more. Arriving at the pick‑up point 15 minutes early avoids missing the bus.
list: Travel in shoulder season (Oct‑Nov or Mar‑Apr) for fewer crowds
Bring a small blanket for the sand‑boarding stop – it can be chilly
Ask for a window seat on the bus for better views and less motion sickness

sections.heading: How to book, save money and downsides
sections.body:
You can book directly on the operator’s website or through NZ family travel partners like nzfamilytravel.co.nz, which sometimes offers a $10‑per‑person discount for newsletter subscribers. Paying by credit card early (within 48 hours) can also snag a 5% discount.

Downsides: the long day can be exhausting for younger kids, the sand‑track is noisy and the bathroom facilities are limited to a single portable toilet on the bus. If your family prefers a shorter outing, consider a half‑day Te Paki dunes only tour instead.
list: Book 2‑3 weeks ahead for the best price
Use a family travel coupon code for $10 off each ticket
Consider a private hire if you need more flexible timing
